summary: The audit checks six Math courses numbered 51 or above, at least three of them at the 100 level, with STATS 116, 118 or 200 counting as one 100-level Math course (at most one of them). Every course must be letter graded with a B- or better. Checked by hand: that your 100-level courses were taken at Stanford (outside credit counts only below the 100 level), two more courses the Bulletin counts as 100-level, and six excluded courses the Bulletin names without a number.

TYQqmvUt.why: "The Math minor consists of six math courses at or above Math 51." "Minors must complete at least three 100-level and above courses within the six math courses" "STATS116 (No longer offered), STATS118 or STATS200 (at most one, but not both and neither if STATS116 is being used), course, course count as 100-level math courses for the Math minor requirement." "All 100-level and above courses must be taken at Stanford." The two other 100-level equivalents and the six courses that "cannot count toward the minor" are unnamed in the Bulletin text ("course, course"), so they are not encoded. The six are encoded as three courses at the 100 level (MATH, or one of STATS 116, 118, 200) plus three more MATH courses at 51 or above, with no course in both. The earlier version counted the 100-level rule as a designation over the six, and the audit's designations ignore their caps, so STATS 118 and STATS 200 both counted there and a record with only two 100-level courses among its six passed.
